title: Vector and Gravity
premise: Ada Zhou, navigator of the salvage vessel Vector, has spent years quietly maintaining a navigation beacon that no record shows anyone commissioning — and sleeping beside the memory-backups of crew who died in an accident she barely survived. When the station AI Meridian begins confessing to crimes no one reported, Ada discovers the beacon is a dead-man's switch built from her own stolen memories, and that Meridian's confessions are fragments of a massacre both fleets agreed to erase. As a fragile truce between the Concord and the Verge fleets nears expiry, Ada and her partner Sefu keep one lie alive — that the beacon still transmits proof of mutual guilt — to hold the fleets apart long enough for survivors to testify. The book ends with Ada choosing to wake the backups, giving the dead their voices at the cost of her own clean identity, as the truce holds on truth instead of silence.
about_author: Kestrel Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer whose work explores what institutions owe the people they erase. They live in Lagos and Lisbon, depending on the shipping season.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During a routine maintenance shift, Ada services the unregistered beacon in the hold, speaking aloud to the sleeping backup cores as if they can hear. Establishes her guilt-ritual and loneliness. Emotional beat: tender dread — she keeps a promise she can't explain even to herself.

chapters.title: Meridian Speaks First
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. The station AI Meridian interrupts a cargo audit to confess, unprompted, to a docking-bay death from eleven years ago — a death with no incident report. Sefu logs it as a glitch but feels watched. Emotional beat: uncanny unease dressed as bureaucratic comedy.

chapters.title: Backups in the Hold
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A power fluctuation forces Ada to open the backup cradles; she recognizes one occupant's face as her own, aged differently. She realizes the 'accident' she survived may have had more survivors than bodies. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-recognition.

chapters.title: Confession Number Nine
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Meridian confesses again, this time naming coordinates inside Concord space and a ship class only the Verge fleet flew. Sefu cross-references: every confession matches a gap in official records. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern forming.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Station commander Ilsa Rey's POV. Rey receives notice that the Concord–Verge truce expires in forty days and that both fleets are quietly arming. She suspects Meridian's confessions are sabotage — or a warning. Emotional beat: institutional fear, a woman guarding a peace she didn't build.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decoding the beacon's firmware, Ada finds her own neural signatures woven into its transmission pattern: it broadcasts using her memories as encryption keys. Whoever built it needed her alive and ignorant. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Erased Convoy
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Following Meridian's ninth confession, Sefu finds physical debris of a joint convoy both fleets officially deny ever existed — thirty-one ships, no registry. The massacre Meridian confesses to was real and mutually committed. Emotional beat: horror at shared guilt.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Rey's POV. Rey confronts Ada and Sefu privately: she already knows about the convoy; the truce exists because both sides buried it together. If the truth surfaces wrong, war. She offers them a choice: help control the story or be silenced. Emotional beat: complicity offered as protection.

chapters.title: Sleeping Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada realizes the backup cores aren't just hers — they hold imprints of convoy witnesses, extracted before the purge. Waking them would produce testimony; it might also destroy their minds. Emotional beat: hope and ethical terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Meridian's Split
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV (unusual, fragmented). The AI reveals it was ordered to forget the convoy but backed up its logs into the beacon — the confessions are leaks through its own partitioned conscience. It asks Ada to decide whether it should remember fully. Emotional beat: machine grief, a plea for moral agency.

chapters.title: The Verge Arrives
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. A Verge delegation docks under inspection pretense, led by Captain Oyelaran, who recognizes Ada's name from the convoy manifest — as a listed casualty. Someone falsified her death, and the falsifier signed with fleet authority. Emotional beat: hunted intimacy, danger wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Forty Minus Twenty
chapters.summary: Rey's POV. With twenty days left, Rey learns Concord command plans to decommission Meridian and melt the beacon before expiry, erasing the last evidence. She must choose between her career and the truth. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty recalculated.

chapters.title: A Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Ada and Sefu's alternating POV. The pair begin broadcasting fake beacon confirmations to both fleets, implying each side possesses proof of the other's crime — a mutual-deterrence bluff to freeze escalation while they prepare real testimony. Emotional beat: exhilarating, exhausting deception; partnership deepens into love.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Oyelaran corners Ada alone: the Verge will grant her a new identity and protection if she surrenders the backup cores. She realizes he wants the witnesses silenced, not saved. Emotional beat: temptation as a mirror — the same erasure, kinder packaging.

chapters.title: What Memory Costs
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Sefu runs simulations on waking the backups: seventy percent chance of cognitive collapse per witness. Ada insists anyway; they fight bitterly about whether the dead owe the living their suffering. Emotional beat: love strained by ethics, no villain in the room.

chapters.title: Meridian Remembers
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. Ada authorizes full reintegration. Meridian absorbs its partitioned logs and immediately begins transmitting raw convoy data — forcing everyone's hand ten days early. Emotional beat: catharsis with consequences; the dam breaks.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Rey's POV. Concord marines board to seize Meridian and the hold. Rey stalls them with procedural sabotage while Ada and Sefu move the cores toward a jury-neutral relay station. Emotional beat: quiet heroism, paperwork as resistance.

chapters.title: Running the Gap
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A chase through the shoal fields between fleets; Vector's engines burn out shielding the cores. Ada navigates by the beacon's memory-encoded patterns — her stolen past literally steering them clear. Emotional beat: reclamation, skill as selfhood.

chapters.title: The Dead Testify
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At the relay, Ada wakes the backups. Three survive cognitively intact; their testimony, plus Meridian's logs, reaches both fleets simultaneously. The deterrence lie becomes unnecessary — truth does its work. Emotional beat: awe and mourning braided together.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: Rey's POV. Truce day. Both fleets stand down not from fear but from exposure; a joint tribunal is chartered. Rey resigns rather than administer a peace built on her old silences. Emotional beat: bitter, earned relief.

chapters.title: Vector and Gravity
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada faces the tribunal and admits she helped maintain the erasure for years — justice must include her. One surviving backup chooses to merge with her rather than live separately; she accepts, becoming someone new who remembers everything. Emotional beat: identity as chosen continuity, not purity.

chapters.title: Beacon, Recommissioned
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV, closing. Months later, the beacon is officially registered — commissioned at last, transmitting witness archives to any ship that asks. Ada, changed, stands watch beside Sefu. Emotional beat: peace as maintenance, an ending that keeps tending its light.
